subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is the observer and strategist who silently grifts the potion of flying using Glabbagool, marks the emotional deception of Bookwyrm, and documents the group's moral compromise — choosing embarrassment over murder as the crime to expose.
source_quote: I lifted the cup, tilted it to my mouth, and let the tea run down into Glabbagool instead of down my throat.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is the manipulative Avowed leader who feigns grief and outrage while secretly relieved that Alkrist’s confession shields her — she orchestrates the group’s isolation, allows the safe to be sealed with incriminating evidence, and ensures her own elevation by appearing cooperative.
source_quote: Alkrist. I could never have imagined it.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan is the proceduralist who regains authority through the group’s actions, claims credit for their findings, and becomes the new First Keeper — his rigid adherence to method blinds him to Bookwyrm’s deception and the stolen evidence.
source_quote: It would seem, Kalan, that your methodology has proven its merit.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is Grygum’s sentient, acid-resistant ooze companion who absorbs liquids and magic, silently steals the potion of flying, and demonstrates nascent discipline by acting only on whispered instruction.
source_quote: Under the skin of my arm, Glabbagool liked the flying skill. He thought it was a good skill.

subject: Fembris Lancer
fact: Fembris Lancer is the passive observer and unwitting taster who, despite being under suspicion, remains naive and trusting — his consumption of the food serves as a risk-spending tool for the party’s survival calculus.
source_quote: Fembris, on the other hand, had no such reservations — come, come, come, already reaching, all appetite and no suspicion.

subject: The Avowed
fact: The Avowed is the governing body of the academic society that has been infiltrated by deception; its members are quick to accept Alkrist’s confession, seal evidence without scrutiny, and elevate Bookwyrm’s authority — revealing systemic complacency and institutional blindness.
source_quote: The Avowed had all decided they'd won.

subject: safe opening
fact: The opening of Alkrist’s safe reveals a potion of flying, healing potion, gold, and a red herring coin — but no direct evidence of guilt, causing the Avowed to shift blame and abandon investigation, allowing Bookwyrm to control the narrative.
source_quote: Nothing else in there implicated Alkrist of anything.

subject: potion of flying
fact: The potion of flying is stolen by Grygum via Glabbagool during the chaos of the safe’s opening, concealed in the ooze, and removed from the scene without detection — becoming the party’s most valuable and hidden asset.
source_quote: While she's talking, my Glabbagool arm swipes the potion of flying off the table.

subject: red herring coin
fact: The red herring coin stamped with a herring is a deliberate red herring placed in Alkrist’s safe to mislead investigators — its presence signals that the owner had nothing to hide, reinforcing the illusion of innocence.
source_quote: One of the gold coins had a herring stamped on it, and the herring was red.

subject: Deneir's Sanctum
fact: Deneir's Sanctum is the book-filled chamber repurposed as a holding cell, where the party is confined under guard — symbolizing their entrapment within Bookwyrm’s narrative despite their successes.
source_quote: They put us in Deneir's office to wait out the evening.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a sentient ooze entity bonded to Grygum, capable of absorbing liquids, resisting acid, and executing silent theft — its behavior reflects training, restraint, and emerging autonomy.
source_quote: He took it. A faint singe of acid, a small heat under the skin of my arm as he burned it away — only I felt it.

subject: Bookwyrm's true guilt
fact: The party possesses no proof that Bookwyrm committed the crime, only Alkrist’s accusation — leaving her guilt unresolved, her power intact, and the group’s moral stance reduced to a quiet grift rather than justice.
source_quote: We know who did it, someone said, and it's not her. Why wouldn't she be elected.

subject: Daral's curse
fact: Daral’s unresolved magical affliction lingers as a moral question — the party delays curing him, revealing their growing detachment and prioritization of self-interest over compassion.
source_quote: Are you guys going to cure me or anything?

subject: after the naming
fact: The official trial and judgment of Alkrist will occur after the naming ceremony, when the new head of the Avowed assumes power — delaying accountability and ensuring Bookwyrm’s influence endures.
source_quote: That will be done after the naming, by the new head of the Avowed.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the theatrical strategist who designs the group’s deception playbook — his obsession with dramatic arcs and closing reveals shapes the party’s actions, even as he fails to recognize their moral erosion.
source_quote: It'd be a good closing — she thought she got away with it, and then: one more thing.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the observational tactician who applies narrative theory to interrogation — he detects the seam in Bookwyrm’s performance and advocates for withholding information to provoke deception, but remains passive in action.
source_quote: My take: be a little shy with the full details, but give enough to make it look like they could tell a story.
